review_candidates.title: Data Centre Network Engineer – Johor Bahru
review_candidates.description: Data Centre Network Engineer – Johor Bahru Location: Johor Bahru, Malaysia Employment: 5 days week, 9am to 6pm, Monday to Friday, 12-month renewable employment term Environment: Data Centre / Mission-Critical Infrastructure About the Role We are looking for a hands-on Data Centre Network Engineer to support network operations within a data centre environment in Johor Bahru. This is a practical, hands-on position combining network troubleshooting and configuration with physical data centre network activities , including fibre/copper patching, cabling, connectivity checks and equipment support. The ideal candidate should be comfortable working both at the CLI and physically inside the data hall . Key Responsibilities Perform day-to-day network operations, troubleshooting and incident resolution. Configure and troubleshoot switches, routers and basic firewall connectivity . Support VLAN configuration, trunking, IP addressing and subnetting . Troubleshoot Layer 2 and Layer 3 connectivity issues. Work with networking concepts such as STP/RSTP, LAG/LACP/EtherChannel and gateway redundancy such as HSRP/VRRP . Perform physical network patching for fibre and copper connections between network devices, servers and patch panels. Install, connect, replace and troubleshoot network cables, SFP/transceiver modules and network equipment . Perform cable tracing, labelling and connectivity verification. Support rack-and-stack, network equipment installation and replacement where required. Verify physical and logical connectivity after network changes or patching activities. Support network migration, maintenance and change activities. Perform troubleshooting and basic fault isolation across Layer 1, Layer 2 and Layer 3 . Follow data centre SOPs, change procedures and safety requirements. Maintain accurate network, cabling and activity documentation. Coordinate with remote network teams, vendors and other data centre teams during incidents and maintenance activities. What We're Looking For Around 2–5+ years of hands-on network / data centre / infrastructure experience . Good knowledge of routing and switching fundamentals . Hands-on experience with VLANs, trunking, subnetting and switch configuration . Good understanding of STP, LAG/LACP and network redundancy/failover . Experience with Cisco, Huawei, H3C, Aruba, Juniper or similar enterprise networking equipment . Basic firewall knowledge; Fortinet, Palo Alto, Check Point or similar exposure is advantageous. Hands-on experience with network patching, structured cabling, fibre and/or copper connectivity. Comfortable working with patch panels, SFPs/transceivers, switches, routers and server/network racks . Able to troubleshoot both physical connectivity and network configuration issues . CCNA or equivalent networking certification is preferred but not mandatory if the candidate can demonstrate strong practical networking knowledge. Comfortable working in a data centre environment and performing hands-on physical activities. Able to support maintenance or network activities outside normal working hours when required. Candidates We Would Particularly Like to Meet You may come from a Network Engineer, Data Centre Network Engineer, Network Support Engineer, NOC Engineer or Data Centre Technician background. We are particularly interested in candidates who can do both sides of the job : Network configuration & troubleshooting + physical patching & cabling. Candidates with experience across Cisco, Huawei, H3C, Aruba, Juniper, Fortinet or other enterprise networking platforms are welcome to apply. This is a hands-on role — candidates must be comfortable with both network configuration/troubleshooting and physical fibre/copper network patching within a data centre environment.

We are looking for a Systems Engineer to connect sensors like aerostats, radars, and cameras into the Navy's communications systems. All that information comes together in an operational picture, the single map that Navy watch teams use to see what is happening at sea. You help make that map complete and trustworthy. What you would do Systems engineering is a lot like solving a puzzle. You take pieces that were never made to fit together and you make them work as one. Day to day, that looks like: Connecting sensors, networks, and software so they talk to each other Working across the whole build: planning it, designing it, coding it, testing it, and keeping it running Turning what the customer needs into clear technical requirements Visiting sites to see what is really there before you design around it Running acceptance tests to prove the system works, then fixing what testing turns up Training the partner teams who will operate and maintain what you install Working with Navy staff, program leads, contractors, and other companies on the team Good systems engineers keep one eye on the big picture and one on the details. review_candidates.location: Abu Dhabi, Abu Dhabi Emirate, United Arab Emirates
review_candidates.description: AI Engineer / Forward Deployed Engineer The Role We are looking for an exceptional AI Engineer / Forward Deployed Engineer to work at the intersection of AI engineering, product development, and government transformation . This is not a traditional software engineering role. You will work directly with government entities to understand how critical services and operations work today, identify where AI can fundamentally change them, and then design, build, and deploy the agentic systems that power the new workflow . The role is approximately equal parts AI Engineer and Forward Deployed / Product Engineer . You need to be comfortable building AI agents and production systems while also sitting with domain experts, understanding complex processes, challenging assumptions, and translating real-world problems into working AI products. The goal isn't simply to automate existing workflows. It is to rewire them for an AI-first world . What You'll Do Build Agentic AI Systems Design, build, and deploy AI agents and multi-agent systems that solve complex, real-world problems. Engineer agentic workflows combining LLMs, tools, APIs, enterprise data and existing systems. Build systems incorporating RAG, tool/function calling, structured outputs, memory, reasoning and orchestration . Develop evaluation frameworks, guardrails and observability to ensure AI systems are reliable and production-ready. Move rapidly from prototype to production, continuously improving systems based on real-world usage. Rewire Government Workflows Embed directly with government entities and domain experts to understand how services and operational processes work today. Map existing workflows, decision points, bottlenecks, hand-offs and dependencies. Identify where AI enables an entirely different way of operating—not simply incremental automation. Re-engineer workflows around AI agents, human judgment and automation. Turn manual, fragmented processes into intelligent, adaptive and increasingly autonomous systems. Understand the underlying domain deeply enough to challenge existing assumptions and redesign how work gets done. Operate as a Product Engineer Translate ambiguous stakeholder problems into clear product and technical requirements. Work directly with users rather than relying solely on predefined specifications. Prototype quickly, put products in front of users and iterate based on feedback. Make pragmatic product decisions balancing user experience, technical feasibility, security and impact . Own solutions end-to-end—from discovering the problem through to deployment, adoption and measurable outcomes. What We're Looking For Strong software engineering fundamentals, ideally with significant experience in Python and modern backend/application development. Hands-on experience building applications using LLMs and Generative AI . Experience building AI agents, agentic workflows, RAG systems or LLM-powered applications . Familiarity with modern AI engineering frameworks and patterns such as LangGraph, LangChain, LlamaIndex, MCP, tool calling and structured generation. Experience integrating AI systems with APIs, databases and enterprise systems. Ability to build production-quality software rather than only notebooks, demos or proofs of concept. Strong product intuition and an ability to turn loosely defined problems into working solutions. Excellent communication skills and confidence working directly with senior stakeholders and domain experts. Comfortable operating in ambiguous environments where the problem may initially be more defined than the solution. What Makes You Exceptional You don't see AI as another feature to bolt onto existing software. You think about how organizations, workflows and products should operate when intelligence becomes a native part of the system . You can move between conversations with government leaders and domain experts, whiteboarding a completely new operating model, and then sitting down with engineers to build the agents, integrations and infrastructure required to make it real. You are equally comfortable asking: "How does this process work today?" and "Why should it work this way at all?" The Mission Governments were largely designed around a world where people had to manually retrieve information, interpret documents, coordinate across departments and execute processes. AI changes that assumption. We want to build systems where AI agents can understand, reason, coordinate and execute—with humans providing oversight and judgment where it matters. This role is about more than deploying AI. It's about rewiring government for an AI-first world. Abu Dhabi based On-site (no remote/hybrid)

Comfortable working in a data centre environment and performing hands-on physical activities. Able to support maintenance or network activities outside normal working hours when required. new_matches.title: AI Engineer / Forward Deployed Engineer
new_matches.location: Abu Dhabi, Abu Dhabi Emirate, United Arab Emirates
new_matches.description: AI Engineer / Forward Deployed Engineer The Role We are looking for an exceptional AI Engineer / Forward Deployed Engineer to work at the intersection of AI engineering, product development, and government transformation . This is not a traditional software engineering role. You will work directly with government entities to understand how critical services and operations work today, identify where AI can fundamentally change them, and then design, build, and deploy the agentic systems that power the new workflow . The role is approximately equal parts AI Engineer and Forward Deployed / Product Engineer . You need to be comfortable building AI agents and production systems while also sitting with domain experts, understanding complex processes, challenging assumptions, and translating real-world problems into working AI products. The goal isn't simply to automate existing workflows. It is to rewire them for an AI-first world . What You'll Do Build Agentic AI Systems Design, build, and deploy AI agents and multi-agent systems that solve complex, real-world problems. Engineer agentic workflows combining LLMs, tools, APIs, enterprise data and existing systems. Build systems incorporating RAG, tool/function calling, structured outputs, memory, reasoning and orchestration . Develop evaluation frameworks, guardrails and observability to ensure AI systems are reliable and production-ready. Move rapidly from prototype to production, continuously improving systems based on real-world usage. Rewire Government Workflows Embed directly with government entities and domain experts to understand how services and operational processes work today. Map existing workflows, decision points, bottlenecks, hand-offs and dependencies. Identify where AI enables an entirely different way of operating—not simply incremental automation. Re-engineer workflows around AI agents, human judgment and automation. Turn manual, fragmented processes into intelligent, adaptive and increasingly autonomous systems. Understand the underlying domain deeply enough to challenge existing assumptions and redesign how work gets done. Operate as a Product Engineer Translate ambiguous stakeholder problems into clear product and technical requirements. Work directly with users rather than relying solely on predefined specifications. Prototype quickly, put products in front of users and iterate based on feedback. Make pragmatic product decisions balancing user experience, technical feasibility, security and impact . Own solutions end-to-end—from discovering the problem through to deployment, adoption and measurable outcomes. What We're Looking For Strong software engineering fundamentals, ideally with significant experience in Python and modern backend/application development. Hands-on experience building applications using LLMs and Generative AI . Experience building AI agents, agentic workflows, RAG systems or LLM-powered applications . Familiarity with modern AI engineering frameworks and patterns such as LangGraph, LangChain, LlamaIndex, MCP, tool calling and structured generation. Experience integrating AI systems with APIs, databases and enterprise systems. Ability to build production-quality software rather than only notebooks, demos or proofs of concept. Strong product intuition and an ability to turn loosely defined problems into working solutions. Excellent communication skills and confidence working directly with senior stakeholders and domain experts. Comfortable operating in ambiguous environments where the problem may initially be more defined than the solution. What Makes You Exceptional You don't see AI as another feature to bolt onto existing software. You think about how organizations, workflows and products should operate when intelligence becomes a native part of the system . You can move between conversations with government leaders and domain experts, whiteboarding a completely new operating model, and then sitting down with engineers to build the agents, integrations and infrastructure required to make it real. You are equally comfortable asking: "How does this process work today?" and "Why should it work this way at all?" The Mission Governments were largely designed around a world where people had to manually retrieve information, interpret documents, coordinate across departments and execute processes. AI changes that assumption. We want to build systems where AI agents can understand, reason, coordinate and execute—with humans providing oversight and judgment where it matters. This role is about more than deploying AI. It's about rewiring government for an AI-first world. Abu Dhabi based On-site (no remote/hybrid)
